title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company other than the Chairman. Subject to the full policy, with closed-period exceptional-circumstances approval from the Chairman and a duty to have dealings notified to ASX by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board. Subject to the same substantive prohibitions as other Directors, but must seek closed-period exceptional-circumstances approval from the Lead Independent Director rather than approving their own dealing.

tiers.name: staff
tiers.description: All staff members of the Company. Subject to the full policy, with closed-period exceptional-circumstances approval from the Chairman and a duty to immediately notify the Company Secretary of dealings.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Associates of Directors and staff and any entities controlled by them; the policy applies directly to their private dealings in the Company's securities.

close of business on the day after announcement of the full year results and dividend

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose additional Closed Periods when considering matters that may require disclosure under its Continuous Disclosure obligations; these are communicated to Directors and staff by the Chairman or Company Secretary. Whether such additional periods are otherwise kept confidential is not addressed.

rules.detail: Derivatives, options, warrants, swaps and other financial products are not named or otherwise addressed anywhere in the policy.
Hedging is not named or addressed anywhere in the policy.
Monetisation arrangements (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not named or addressed.
Short selling is not named or addressed anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named or addressed anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are not named or addressed anywhere in the policy.

Outright ban on entering margin lending arrangements against Company securities held. No exceptional-circumstances route applies to this restriction (Exceptional Circumstances in section E is limited to dealing during Closed Periods).
rules.evidence: must not deal in the Company’s securities in the following circumstances: ... For short term trading or speculative purposes and must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on granting security over Company securities held, not limited to margin lending arrangements; no carve-out for other types of security and no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route provided.
rules.evidence: must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.

rules.detail: The prohibition covers both margin lending and granting security more generally, so any secured financing arrangement using Company securities as collateral is banned outright, with no approval pathway.
rules.evidence: must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.

rules.detail: Dealing for short term trading or speculative purposes is prohibited; no minimum holding period is quantified and no carve-outs are stated.
rules.evidence: must not deal in the Company’s securities in the following circumstances: ... For short term trading or speculative purposes

exceptions.evidence: Transfers of securities to a close family member (spouse, civil partner, child, stepchild or other close family member)
Transfers of securities as a contribution to a superannuation fund in which they are a beneficiary
Participation in an offer made to all or most shareholders, including but not limited to the Dividend Reinvestment Plan, a share purchase plan, rights issue ... or equal access buy-back
Transfers of Company securities that result in no change in beneficial ownership

Indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party, and that happens to hold Company securities as part of its portfolio

Where they are a trustee of a trust – the trading of Company securities by that trust, provided they are not a beneficiary of the trust and that any decisions to trade are made independently by other trustees or managers of the trust.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or Lead Independent Director for the Chairman's own dealing)
Chairman (or Lead Independent Director for the Chairman's own dealing)

exemption_authority: Chairman (or, for the Chairman's own dealing, the Lead Independent Director) may grant prior written permission to deal during a Closed Period only in exceptional circumstances (e.g. severe financial hardship or a court-ordered transaction); all approvals are notified to the Company Secretary and the Board. No exemption route is provided for the ban on granting security or entering margin lending arrangements, nor for dealing while possessing material non-public information.

bespoke_clauses.topic: blanket security/margin ban with no carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no carve-out for non-margin secured financing; granting any security interest over the shares (the loan leg of a funded collar) is banned outright for Directors, staff and their associates, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route available for this restriction.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no general preclearance outside closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors (other than the Chairman) and staff may seek prior written permission to deal in the Company’s securities during the Closed Periods from the Chairman, but only in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Closed Periods there is no general preclearance or notification-before-trading requirement (only the post-trade disclosure duty in section F), so dealing in the derivative legs of a collar outside a Closed Period, absent material non-public information, is not gated by a formal approval process under this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and staff must not deal in the Company’s securities in the following circumstances: ... For short term trading or speculative purposes and must not grant security or enter into margin lending arrangements against Company securities held.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy never mentions derivatives, options, swaps, CFDs or hedging, so whether entering an OTC put/call is a 'dealing' subject to the Closed Period and inside-information prohibitions is untested; this should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before relying on the policy's silence.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If their trading activity materially conflicts with the Company’s trading activity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a listed investment company, AUI's own trading book could create a distinct conflict-of-interest constraint if the collar counterparty bank trades the same securities AUI holds.

summary: The loan leg of a funded collar is fatal under this policy: section B.3 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on granting security or entering margin lending arrangements against Company securities held, with no carve-out for non-margin secured financing and no exceptional-circumstances relief available for this restriction, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares cannot be implemented. The policy is silent on derivatives, options and hedging altogether, so the put and call legs alone are not expressly regulated beyond the general prohibitions on dealing while possessing material non-public information, dealing during the two annual Closed Periods (unless the Chairman, or the Lead Independent Director for the Chairman, grants exceptional-circumstances approval), and dealing for short-term or speculative purposes. Outside a Closed Period there is no general preclearance requirement, only a post-trade notification duty to the Company Secretary. Because the funded structure inherently requires pledging the shares as collateral, a funded collar with a bank is not possible under this policy regardless of vesting state or timing; an unfunded collar (derivatives only, no security granted) would face no express bar but its treatment as a 'dealing' is untested and should be confirmed with the Company Secretary.
